structural_remedies.description: Enforce IBAN format validation at payment capture and reject malformed IBANs before bank submission, eliminating FAILED_IBAN_FORMAT refunds.
structural_remedies.rationale: Configurable validation rule can be deployed in payment-db within the remaining 225 minutes; payment-db is healthy and no constraints block the change.; residual gap: Some refund-related tickets may persist due to missing self‑service refund status information or policy clarity, not IBAN errors. proposal.summary: IBAN format errors in payment processing cause customers to submit refund inquiries, increasing ticket volume [E-02][E-01]. The problem was established by observing 900 tickets with a median response time of 2 hours (E-01) and five payment‑db refund failures due to IBAN format errors (E-02), supplemented by stakeholder perception of delay (E-03). The release provides the notify_customer_refund_status action for SH‑SUP and the monitor_ticket_volume action for ticket‑db. The release decision is RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION because the DEFINE gate returned CONDITIONAL_PASS, deferring validation of IBAN format (VOB-U-01), the release scope lacks the validate_iban_format action to address the root cause (semantic:root_coverage), the bank‑api tool is degraded, and open VOBs block the unfinished scope.
